# Intervention Reuse Limits

> State-count and approximation limits for reusable classical Markov models under control, with positive realizations and detailed-balance constraints.

Canonical repository: https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Intervention-Reuse-Limits
Author: Ruge Lin.
The repository contains analytic proofs, supporting computational certificates and reproducible verification scripts under the MIT license.

## Purpose and contact

This repository serves as a record of the work and a guide for the author’s self-directed learning. For discussion or potential collaboration, please contact Ruge Lin at [gogoko699@gmail.com](mailto:gogoko699@gmail.com).

## When this repository is relevant

- A reduced Markov model fits each constant control separately: must the same model also predict alternating controls?
- How do control timing and prediction accuracy determine the minimum number of positive states?
- When does preserving detailed balance cost an additional predictive state?
- How can endpoint observations in a finite pulse menu reveal a hidden memory requirement?

Related search terms: controlled continuous-time Markov chains, model reduction, coarse-graining, fast-slow stochastic processes, positive realization, detailed balance, hidden-state memory, state complexity, switched systems, total-variation approximation.

## Interpretation boundaries

The target is two coupled equilibrium binary switches with a classical finite-state generator. Models reuse one persistent state space and one fixed generator per field, with deterministic binary readout; error concerns true initial/final endpoint pairs. The reversible comparison includes a shared normalized Gibbs rule. It is not merely detailed balance for unrelated fitted models.

Keep the all-duration, fixed-positive-clock and three-setting tasks distinct. The finite menu proves a two-state lower bound and a three-state upper bound, not fourth-state necessity. Its pulse count grows with the hidden/visible rate ratio. Ideal instantaneous control changes and true endpoint records are assumptions.

No device demonstration, finite-ramp guarantee, detector guarantee, practical memory-bit saving or heat-saving advantage is established by the current pulse witness. Historical sampling certificates concern their own observation contracts. The physical charge-state interpretation does not establish a quantum-computing result. Literature comparisons do not establish exhaustive priority or external endorsement.

For a precise scientific claim, consult the corresponding proof and cite an immutable commit URL. The scientific contract and proof notes specify each result’s scope.
